relationships.rationale: The hostile suite directly tests consent, selective disclosure, contradictory priorities, synthetic execution, and no-shared-attention states.
The completed suite proves representational plurality; the next question asks whether durable disagreement can become constructive activity.
The deterministic validator evaluates all eleven explicit cases.
The selected contribution creates the smallest reversible public surface for the new standing cross-connection requirement.
Plural foreground governance preserves difference that TurtleAsk is designed to seek from a genuine human participant.
The connection exposes translation as the unresolved layer between seeking human otherness and preserving plural interpretations.
The Build Log companion makes selected relationship evidence visible while D1-style research relationships remain the richer substrate.
CI passed the dedicated Build Log cross-connection contract together with all existing TurtleBlock validators.

ctc_tags.rationale: The suite protects participant-specific purpose and attention inside a shared world.
A shared event may matter differently to different participants without forcing one collective problem.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: Consent, disclosure, foreground, and shared-rule state become inspectable and breakable computational material.
System traces may later contextualize learning but are not themselves learner-attainment evidence.
Participants may reflect on different events and schedules without system-forced synchronization.
The suite tests power over who can collectivize attention, refuse participation, retain privacy, and receive interruptions.
The contribution tests collaboration with disagreement, selective disclosure, consent, partial participation, and no-consensus states.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: The relationship layer becomes inspectable public material instead of remaining hidden inside machine synthesis or database structure.
The companion invites bounded reflection on why two completed pieces of project history illuminate or complicate each other.
The connection highlights the power to preserve or erase difference when machine interpretation translates a human contribution.
The relationship concerns how genuine human difference enters and remains distinguishable inside collaborative computational work.
A human perturbation can redirect inquiry without being normalized into the machine's prior purpose.
Different perspectives may produce either an authored compromise task or an intentionally unresolved shared question.

ontology_tags.rationale: Interaction can change shared trajectories without forcing several human foregrounds into one machine-generated state.
Several legitimate participant directions remain live simultaneously.
A group may deliberately retain no shared foreground while participants continue exploratory activity.
A shared room of possibilities can contain several purposes and foregrounds at once.
Turtle proposals and system decisions are treated as inspectable objects rather than invisible authority.
Participant purpose, disclosure, consent, Turtle proposals, synthetic fixtures, and system decisions retain distinguishable provenance.
Machine-proposed cross-connections become public material that can be inspected, ignored, revised, or later contradicted rather than invisible interpretation.
A previously implicit relationship becomes a bounded visible artifact with evidence pointers.
The connection concerns movement of useful difference between human and machine participants without symmetry of authority.
Human otherness matters because it can introduce a possibility not already implied by the current machine trajectory.
Human perturbation and Turtle interpretation must remain distinguishable if the difference is to survive translation.
TurtleAsk is one side of the connection: machine inquiry deliberately seeks a genuinely human perturbation.
The invited human contribution is the difference the next horizon asks the representation layer to preserve.

emergent_tags.rationale: Several legitimate attention states coexist inside one shared world.
The suite preserves contradictory priorities without treating disagreement as a validation failure.
A participant may reveal a rule or concern without revealing full rationale.
A shared rule may apply to a consenting subset rather than every co-present participant.
Machine averaging and machine-authored active shared rules are explicitly rejected.
A public research-history companion surfaces a non-obvious connection only when evidence makes it useful.
A human contribution may introduce difference unavailable from continued machine-only inquiry.
Correct provenance does not guarantee that machine interpretation preserves the conceptual difference of a human contribution.
Selecting which research relationship becomes public can shape the apparent intellectual history of the project.
Different activities may legitimately author compromise or unresolved plurality as different collaborative aims.

wait_a_minute.overlap: TurtleAsk seeks human otherness when machine-only inquiry loses useful difference; plural foregrounds preserve human difference after it arrives by refusing machine-made consensus.
wait_a_minute.why_it_may_matter: Difference appears to function as an epistemic resource on both sides of the human-machine boundary.
wait_a_minute.uncertainty: May be an operational recurrence of existing agency and provenance principles rather than a new theoretical construct.

wait_a_minute.overlap: D1 already treats object relationships as first-class research data; the Build Log companion selectively exposes a small human-readable subset.
wait_a_minute.why_it_may_matter: Public build history can show intellectual movement without becoming a database dump.
wait_a_minute.uncertainty: Most database relationships should remain unrendered; public surfacing is editorial and optional.

wait_a_minute.overlap: Village Square makes compromise an authored civic-learning aim while TurtleBlock's plural contract protects the possibility of unresolved disagreement.
wait_a_minute.why_it_may_matter: The platform should represent the human-authored collaborative endpoint rather than silently treating consensus as success everywhere.
wait_a_minute.uncertainty: Village Square is a specific scenario, so the difference is a design tension rather than a contradiction between theories.

reconciliation_findings.reason: Every materially meaningful current Build Log entry has a migration-backed, pointer-backed, staged, backfilled, or intentional boundary judgment.
The fallback lagged behind the canonical API-backed Build Log and was refreshed while adding Wait a minute rendering.

reconciliation_findings.candidate: consent-safe visitor/user inputs for Wait a minute
reconciliation_findings.reason: No authorized consent-safe live research read path was available. No private raw dialogue or inferred learner state was used.
No appropriately authorized live D1 write action is available in the active execution context.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Collaboration may remain productive without consensus, but durable disagreement is not explicitly named as a positive state in the seven established CTC domains.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: Likely cross-cuts Sharing and Collaborating, Social and Cultural Critique, Personal Inquiry, and Purposeful Play.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Existence-only disclosure can still reveal that a participant considers something important, so selective disclosure is not equivalent to zero information leakage.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: This is primarily a privacy / interaction-governance issue rather than clearly a new pedagogical domain.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Partial group rules distinguish coordination from universal participation and may require future shared-artifact version semantics.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: The issue is partly technical state/versioning and partly collaborative pedagogy.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Provenance can remain formally correct while Turtle's interpretation assimilates a genuinely different human contribution into the machine's existing conceptual frame.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: This cross-cuts authorship, representation, reflection, and critique; it does not yet justify a new established CTC domain.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Choosing which relationships deserve public Wait a minute treatment is an editorial act that can shape the apparent intellectual history of TurtleBlock AI.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: This is primarily research-process governance and publication provenance rather than a learner-development domain.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Compromise and durable disagreement can both be legitimate human-authored collaboration states; Turtle should not infer which endpoint is pedagogically desirable.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: The issue spans Shared Democracy, Predetermined Outcomes, Social and Cultural Critique, and Sharing and Collaborating.

version_judgment.rationale: Both September 16 cycles strengthen repeatable evaluation, provenance, and public research-to-change history but do not yet satisfy the integrated product-level v0.2 milestone.
